# betadiversity

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

betadiversity computes Whittaker's multiplicative (`beta_M`) and Lande's
additive (`beta_A`) beta diversity from site x species presence/absence data,
with analytical confidence intervals and a two-sample hypothesis test,
following Kiflawi & Spencer (2004, *Ecology* 85(10):2895-2900). True regional
richness (gamma) is estimated via the first-order jackknife estimator rather
than assumed equal to observed richness, which is what gives the confidence
intervals and hypothesis test their validity.

## Installation

betadiversity is not yet on CRAN or GitHub. Until then, install it from a
local clone with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install("path/to/betadiversity")
```

## Example

Raw field data usually comes as one row per observation (a site, a species,
and optionally a detection value and a habitat/category label).
`as_site_by_species()` reshapes that into the sites x species matrix that
`beta_diversity()` expects:

```{r example}
library(betadiversity)

records <- data.frame(
  site = c("s1", "s1", "s2", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s4"),
  species = c("sp1", "sp2", "sp1", "sp3", "sp2", "sp1", "sp3"),
  seen = c("Y", "Y", "yes", "N", "Y", "Y", "yes"),
  habitat = c("tree", "tree", "tree", "tree", "open", "open", "open")
)

res <- as_site_by_species(records, site = "site", species = "species",
                           value = "seen", group = "habitat",
                           all_sites = paste0("s", 1:4))
res$x

beta_diversity(res$x, group = res$group)
```

Two independent site-sets can be compared directly with
`beta_diversity_test()`, which returns a two-sample Z-test on both `beta_M`
and `beta_A` (Eqs. 10a-10b of Kiflawi & Spencer 2004):

```{r test-example}
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rbinom(8 * 10, 1, 0.35), nrow = 8)
y <- matrix(rbinom(8 * 10, 1, 0.35), nrow = 8)
beta_diversity_test(x, y)
```

See `vignette("betadiversity")` for a fuller walkthrough of the jackknife
estimator and what the two beta diversity measures mean.

## Citation

If you use betadiversity, please cite the method it implements:

> Kiflawi, M., & Spencer, M. (2004). Confidence intervals and hypothesis
> testing for beta diversity. *Ecology*, 85(10), 2895-2900.
